name: Hunter's Bestiary
description: Monsters and lore from Vaelor's bestiary project.

lore.summary: The annis is the brute matriarch of the hag kind — blue-black skinned, iron-thewed, with a beauty she borrows and a cruelty she owns. She lairs near roads and villages, wearing a fair face by day to lure travellers, lone children, and trusting men into reach of her true arms.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Larger than a man — a tall, long-limbed giant of a hag.
Durability: Sturdy; she weathers many blows before she falls.
Defenses: Iron-hard skin; blade and arrow scarcely mark her, and some spells slip from her unspent.
Speed: Quicker on her feet than she looks.
Might: Tremendously strong; her grip pins, and her claws rend flesh from bone.
Mind: Cunning and patient — clever enough to wear a fair disguise and lay a trap.
Disposition: A predator of the lonely road; she lures rather than charges, and strikes once you trust her.
Bane: Crushing force, where blade and arrow fail.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: She comes in friendly guise, then seizes a single victim in both clawed hands. Once she has hold she rakes again and again, and if both claws bite home she tears a terrible wound. She fights to pin and kill one quarry at a time rather than face a crowd.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Bring a hammer, not your good sword. Learned that the wet way.
• Never let her get a grip — break free at once, or she'll rake the same poor soul to ribbons.
• She wears a fair face on the road. The hands give her away first; keep your distance.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: She will talk — sweetly, and in a borrowed face. I have parleyed with an annis twice; both times the words were bait. Speak if you must, but out of arm's reach, and count your companions.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:

Rend: An annis that hits with both claw attacks latches onto the opponent’s body and tears the flesh. This attack automatically deals an extra 2d6+10 points of damage.

Spell-Like Abilities: 3/day—disguise self, fog cloud. Caster level 8th.

lore.summary: Not every horned thing on the hunter's list is a monster of malice. The centaur is a proud, often peaceful folk of the deep wood and open plain — but a threatened or maddened centaur is a wall of muscle that gallops, looses arrows, and tramples in a single breath.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a man's torso atop the body of a full warhorse.
Durability: No tougher than a strong warrior; concentrated blows fell it.
Defenses: Wears hide armour and bears a shield, but no monstrous toughness.
Speed: Gallops faster than any foot-soldier can run.
Might: Strong; hooves break bone, and it fights with bow and blade at once.
Mind: Simple but no fool — a proud, often peaceable folk.
Disposition: Frequently no enemy at all — wary and territorial, dangerous only when threatened or maddened.
Bane: Open ground is its strength; broken ground, its undoing.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It opens at distance with the bow, then wheels in to trample with both hooves while striking with sword or spear — using its speed to choose when to close and when to flee.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Half these 'kills' should've been conversations. Mind its temper before you draw. –the Warden
• Bait them into the trees — no room to gallop, no trample.
• Don't dawdle at bowshot; close hard, or stay well out of it.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Proud folk, not monsters. Approach with weapons slung and greet them plainly; most quarrels with centaurs are of our own making. I have shared their fires. Fight only if honour — or drink — turns them.

lore.summary: The doppelganger is the hunter's nightmare made flesh: a thing with no true face that wears yours, your captain's, your lover's. It reads the mind, mirrors the manner, and slides into a household to feed on trust before it ever raises a hand.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Man-sized in its true shape.
Durability: Frail in a straight fight — deception is its strength, not endurance.
Defenses: Unarmoured; no special toughness.
Speed: As a man.
Might: Modest; a single weak blow from a shapeless fist.
Mind: Sharp and devious — it reads the surface of your thoughts to wear the face you trust.
Disposition: An infiltrator, not a brawler; it replaces and deceives, killing only when cornered.
Bane: True sight and divination strip any shape it wears.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It rarely fights openly. It takes the shape of someone you trust, lives among you, and acts only when exposed — then lashes out with a shapeless blow and tries to flee or sow confusion among allies who can't tell friend from forgery.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Ask it about the night we lost Haln. It won't know. Nobody alive but me does.
• If 'someone' is suddenly very keen on the vault keys, look twice.
• Sleep and charm are wasted on it. Force a plain fight — it can barely swing a fist.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: It talks as well as any man; that is the weapon. Every word buys it time to learn you. It values its skin, though, and will often bargain to withdraw rather than die as someone else.

Change Shape: A doppelganger can assume the shape of any Small or Medium humanoid. In humanoid form, the doppelganger loses its natural attacks. A doppelganger can remain in its humanoid form until it chooses to assume a new one. A change in form cannot be dispelled, but a doppelganger reverts to its natural form when killed. A true seeing spell or ability reveals its natural form.

lore.summary: A cruel, slow-witted predator of stone, the gargoyle perches motionless on ledge and battlement until prey wanders beneath. It delights in patience — and in the moment the 'carving' opens its eyes.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Man-sized, but built of what looks like grotesque stone.
Durability: Hardy for its size.
Defenses: Its stony hide shrugs off ordinary weapons almost entirely.
Speed: No faster than a man afoot, but it flies well and strikes from above.
Might: Strong claws, bite and horns; dangerous in a flurry.
Mind: Dull and cruel — easily baited, easily led into a trap.
Disposition: A patient ambusher that perches stone-still as a carving until prey wanders beneath.
Bane: Enchanted steel; common iron will not bite.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It freezes among statuary until you pass, then drops to rake with its claws and lifts back out of reach between passes — wearing you down from the air.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Every damned statue on that roof. One of them blinked.
• No enchanted blade? Then you brought a stick. Don't.
• Ground it if you can — half the monster out of the air. Its drowned cousin the kapoacinth is the same beast.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: It can speak, though it seldom cares to. Cruelty amuses it; coin sometimes moves it. I once bought passage beneath a bridge of them for a sack of silver. Expect it to renege.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

lore.summary: The green hag haunts fen, bog, and drowned wood, a malicious schemer who poisons wells, blights crops, and whispers folk toward ruin. She fights with claw and a withering touch, but her true craft is misdirection — false voices in the reeds, invisible passage, and a fair face when one suits her.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Man-sized, gaunt and sinewy.
Durability: Tougher than she looks; takes a fair beating.
Defenses: Some spells slip off her witch-nature; her flesh is otherwise unarmoured.
Speed: Quick on land and a strong swimmer.
Might: Surprisingly strong claws — and a touch that saps the strength from a living body.
Mind: A cunning schemer; she poisons wells, blights land, and whispers folk toward ruin.
Disposition: A manipulator and ambusher — she isolates one victim with trickery before she ever shows a claw.
Bane: Denied her withering touch, she is but a clawed crone.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: She uses false voices and invisibility to split a party and corner one victim, drains the strength from them with a withering touch, then claws them down. Misdirection first, violence last.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• She'll call out in your own brother's voice. He's already dead. Don't go. –the Warden
• Don't let her lay a hand on you — a couple of touches and your strongest can't lift his axe.
• Bring light and a way to reveal the unseen; she fights from hiding.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: She loves talk the way an angler loves the worm, and she will mimic voices you trust. Converse only to learn her terms — a hag's bargain always costs more than the fight would have.

Mimicry: A green hag can imitate the sounds of almost any animal found near its lair.

lore.summary: Filthy, cruel, and beautiful only in voice, the harpy nests on sea-cliffs and ruined towers. Its song is its hunt: a haunting melody that draws the spellbound off the path — and off the edge — into talon's reach.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Man-sized — a foul bird's body with a hag's torso and head.
Durability: Frail; once you weather the song, it dies fast.
Defenses: Unarmoured and lightly built.
Speed: Clumsy on foot, swift and agile on the wing.
Might: Weak in talon and club — its true weapon is its voice.
Mind: Cruel and low, but cunning enough to sing the unwary off a cliff.
Disposition: A lure-predator; it captivates with song and feeds on the helpless.
Bane: Deafness; the song needs ears to work.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It sings a haunting melody that draws the spellbound stumbling toward it — often off a ledge — then clubs and claws the helpless. Pressed, it simply flies out of reach and sings again.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Beeswax in the ears. Ugly, simple, saves your life.
• If your mate starts walking toward the singing, tackle him. Apologise later.
• Shake the song once and you're safe from it — then drop it before it flies off.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Do not listen, let alone speak. Her song is the conversation, and it ends with you walking willingly into her claws. Stop your ears and strike.

A creature that successfully saves cannot be affected again by the same harpy’s song for 24 hours. The save DC is Charisma-based.

lore.summary: The kapoacinth is the gargoyle of the deep — the same patient stone predator, but webbed and gilled, lurking on reefs, drowned ruins, and harbor pilings. Sailors who dive for a 'fallen statue' rarely surface.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Man-sized, stony-hided, finned for the deep.
Durability: Hardy for its size.
Defenses: Stone-like hide turns aside mundane weapons.
Speed: Slow on land, swift and at home underwater.
Might: Strong claws, bite and horns.
Mind: Dull and cruel, like its land cousin.
Disposition: An underwater ambusher that hangs frozen on reef or piling until prey swims near.
Bane: Enchanted steel, and dry land.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It poses as crusted stone on a reef or pier until you're close, then rakes up from below — where your footing and your breath are already against you.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Same beast as the gargoyle, just drowned. Same rule: no enchanted blade, no fight.
• Never follow one down. The water is its trophy room, not yours.
• Tap the 'statues' on the pilings before they tap you.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: As its cousin of the rooftops, but wave-dwelling: brutish, greedy, half-willing to bargain. Underwater there is no talking anyway. On land, coin first, blade ready.

It is identical to a gargoyle in every way except that it has a swim speed of 60 feet in place of the gargoyle’s fly speed, gains the aquatic subtype, breathes water, and dwells in seas, sunken ruins, and coastal caves rather than on land.

lore.summary: The medusa needs no army; her face is the weapon. Lairs are easy to read — the frozen mid-stride figures of those who looked once too long. She is cunning, often charming at a distance, and uses the bow to soften foes who avert their eyes.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Woman-sized.
Durability: Frail once her gaze is answered.
Defenses: Lightly protected; no special toughness.
Speed: As a person.
Might: Slight in body — her power is in her eyes, not her arms.
Mind: Cunning; often charming at a distance, and she'll soften eyes-averted foes with a bow.
Disposition: She forces you to choose between looking and fighting blind; her lairs are littered with the petrified.
Bane: An averted eye or a mirror breaks her gaze.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: She manoeuvres so a careful, eyes-down foe must either meet her gaze and risk turning to stone or fight half-blind — and she peppers the cautious with arrows. Her serpent hair bites with venom for any who come too close.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• The statues in the doorway ARE the warning. Read the room before you read her face. –the Warden
• Shield-polish is cheap. A stone hunter is a lawn ornament.
• Keep clear of her hair — the snakes carry venom even when the eyes miss.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: She converses gladly — often veiled, often courteous. I once spoke with one for an hour, eyes fixed on her shadow, and left with my life and a map. Never her eyes. If the veil drops mid-sentence, the talk is over.

lore.summary: Bull-headed, foul-tempered, and built like a battering ram, the minotaur rules twisting tunnels and ruined labyrinths by sheer ferocity. It hunts by smell, charges to open, then hews with a greataxe few can survive trading blows against.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a bull-headed brute that towers over a man.
Durability: Solid; it trades blows well and weathers a beating.
Defenses: Thick hide and shaggy fur, but no armour that turns a good blow.
Speed: As fast as a man, with a devastating charge.
Might: Immense — a greataxe in its hands and horns that gore on the charge.
Mind: Dull and savage, but it cannot be lost or mazed; it owns the labyrinth.
Disposition: Foul-tempered and territorial; it charges to open, then stands and hews.
Bane: Robbed of its charge, it is only a brute.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It opens with a goring charge that can fell a strong man outright, then settles into trading greataxe blows — and in its twisting tunnels it never loses the scent or the way.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• It can't get lost. You can. Don't chase it into the maze.
• Caltrops in the corridor. No run-up, no death-gore.
• Once it can't charge, pile on together — it's out of tricks.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: It has words, but the labyrinth-rage eats them. By the time you hear its breath it is already charging. Save your speeches.

Natural Cunning: Although minotaurs are not especially intelligent, they possess innate cunning and logical ability. This gives them immunity to maze spells, prevents them from ever becoming lost, and enables them to track enemies. Further, they are never caught flat-footed.

lore.summary: The most wretched of the hag kind, the sea hag is grotesque even among monsters — so hideous her mere visage withers the strong. She haunts coast, reef, and salt marsh, drowning sailors and souring the catch out of spite.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Man-sized, grotesque and gangly.
Durability: Very frail — among the easiest to fell IF you can face her.
Defenses: Some spells slip off her; her body is otherwise weak.
Speed: Quick on land, a strong swimmer.
Might: Strong claws, but her true weapon is how she looks.
Mind: Spiteful and low-cunning; she drowns sailors and sours the catch out of malice.
Disposition: Hostile and wretched; her mere visage withers the brave.
Bane: Her horror works only on those who see her.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: She closes just enough for her hideous visage to sap the strength from any who look at her, fixes a baleful eye on the strongest, then claws the weakened. Her face does most of the killing.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Ugly enough to kill. That's not a figure of speech with this one. –the Warden
• Frail as a wet reed — IF you don't look at her. Answer the gaze and one volley ends her.
• Don't chase her into deep water; make her come to the shallows.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Nothing in her wants conversation; her very face is an assault. She may croak a curse at you — that is not parley. Strike or flee.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Monstrous Humanoid (Aquatic)
Initiative: +1
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares), swim 40 ft.
Armor Class: 14 (+1 Dex, +3 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 13
Base Attack/Grapple: +3/+7
Attack: Claw +7 melee (1d4+4)
Full Attack: 2 claws +7 melee (1d4+4)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Horrific appearance, evil eye
Special Qualities: Amphibious, spell resistance 14
Saves: Fort +2, Ref +4, Will +4
Abilities: Str 19, Dex 12, Con 12, Int 10, Wis 13, Cha 14
Skills: Craft or Knowledge (any one) +3, Hide +4, Listen +6, Spot +6, Swim +12
Feats: Alertness, Toughness
Environment: Temperate aquatic
Organization: Solitary or covey (3 hags of any kind plus 1–8 ogres and 1–4 evil giants)
Challenge Rating: 4
Alignment: Usually chaotic evil

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Horrific Appearance: The sight of a sea hag is so revolting that anyone (other than another hag) who sets eyes upon one must succeed on a DC 13 Fortitude save or instantly be weakened, taking 2d6 points of Strength damage. This damage cannot reduce a victim’s Strength score below 0, but anyone reduced to Strength 0 is helpless.

Evil Eye: Three times per day, a sea hag can cast its dire gaze upon any single creature within 30 feet. The target must succeed on a DC 13 Will save or be dazed for three days, although remove curse or dispel evil can restore sanity sooner. In addition, an affected creature must succeed on a DC 13 Fortitude save or die from fright.

Amphibious: Although sea hags are aquatic, they can survive indefinitely on land.

lore.summary: Apply the vampire's curse to a large monstrous host and you get a horror the school files under your favored quarry: faster, stronger, undying, and far cleverer than the thing it was in life. It commands lesser creatures, drains the life from warriors with a touch, and bends the weak-willed to its service.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — built on an ogre-sized host, and far worse than it was in life.
Durability: Does not die in a fair fight; it knits its wounds in moments and refuses to stay down.
Defenses: Ordinary weapons barely tell — it shrugs off unsilvered, unenchanted steel and laughs at cold and lightning.
Speed: Faster and stronger than the living thing it once was; it scales sheer walls and melts into mist.
Might: Tremendous — a touch drains the very life and years from a warrior.
Mind: Cleverer than the brute it was made from; patient, because it has forever.
Disposition: A predator and a tyrant; it commands lesser beasts and bends the weak-willed to its will.
Bane: Sunlight and running water destroy it; a stake pins it in its coffin.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It seizes the strongest mind and turns your ally against you, drains the life from warriors with a touch, and summons rats, bats and wolves. Threatened, it dissolves into mist and retreats to its coffin to heal. It never fights fair because it never has to.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Killing it in the hall just sends it home to heal. The COFFIN is the kill. Always the coffin. –the Warden
• It can't cross running water alone — use the river. A presented holy symbol holds it back.
• Ward against its draining touch and its eye before you close, or it turns your champion against you.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: He will insist on talking — he was a man once, and misses an audience. Parley flatters him and may buy you the night. But his eyes work on you while you listen: watch his chin, keep the door at your back, and accept no hospitality.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor threat

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: The base creature’s type changes to undead (augmented humanoid or monstrous humanoid); size is unchanged
Initiative: As base creature, improved by the Dexterity increase and the bonus Improved Initiative feat
Speed: Same as the base creature
Armor Class: The base creature’s natural armor bonus improves by +6
Base Attack/Grapple: As the base creature (do not recalculate base attack bonus); grapple improves with the +6 Strength
Attack: Retains all the base creature’s attacks and gains a slam attack if it had none
Full Attack: Slam or natural weapons; if armed, weapon as primary with slam or other natural weapon as secondary
Space/Reach: Same as the base creature
Special Attacks: Blood drain, children of the night, dominate, create spawn, energy drain (save DC 10 + 1/2 vampire’s level + Cha modifier)
Special Qualities: Alternate form, damage reduction 10/silver and magic, fast healing 5, gaseous form, resistance to cold 10 and electricity 10, spider climb, +4 turn resistance, undead traits
Saves: As the base creature (not recalculated), plus undead immunities
Abilities: Str +6, Dex +4, Int +2, Wis +2, Cha +4; no Constitution score
Skills: +8 racial bonus on Bluff, Hide, Listen, Move Silently, Search, Sense Motive, and Spot; otherwise as base creature
Feats: Gains Alertness, Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Improved Initiative, and Lightning Reflexes
Environment: Any, usually same as base creature
Organization: Solitary, pair, gang (3–5), or troupe (1–2 plus 2–5 vampire spawn)
Challenge Rating: Same as the base creature +2
Alignment: Always evil (any)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Blood Drain (Ex): A vampire can suck blood from a living victim with its fangs by making a successful grapple check. If it pins the foe, it drains blood, dealing 1d4 points of Constitution drain each round the pin is maintained. Each such successful attack leaves the vampire briefly invigorated.

Children of the Night (Su): Once per day a vampire can call forth 1d6+1 rat swarms, 1d4+1 bat swarms, or a pack of 3d6 wolves as a standard action. (A non-terrestrial base creature might summon other creatures of similar power.) They arrive in 2d6 rounds and serve the vampire for up to 1 hour.

Dominate (Su): A vampire can crush an opponent’s will by looking into his or her eyes. This is similar to a gaze attack, except the vampire must use a standard action and those merely looking at it are unaffected. A target must succeed on a Will save or fall under the vampire’s influence as though by dominate person (caster level 12th). Range 30 feet.

Create Spawn (Su): A humanoid or monstrous humanoid slain by a vampire’s energy drain rises as a vampire spawn 1d4 days after burial. If instead the victim’s Constitution is drained to 0, weaker victims return as spawn and mightier ones as full vampires. Spawn are enslaved to their creator until the master is destroyed; a vampire can enslave only a limited number.

Energy Drain (Su): Living creatures hit by a vampire’s slam attack (or any other natural weapon it possesses) gain two negative levels. Each negative level bestowed leaves the vampire momentarily bolstered. A vampire can use its energy drain ability once per round.

Alternate Form (Su): A vampire can assume the shape of a bat, dire bat, wolf, or dire wolf as a standard action, similar to polymorph cast by a 12th-level character except that it heals no injury by changing form and must choose among these forms. In alternate form it loses its slam and dominate but gains the new form’s natural weapons and extraordinary attacks, lasting until it changes again or until sunrise.

Damage Reduction (Su): A vampire has damage reduction 10/silver and magic. Its natural weapons are treated as magic weapons for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Fast Healing (Ex): A vampire heals 5 points of damage each round so long as it is not yet incapacitated. If struck down in combat it automatically assumes gaseous form and flees; it must reach its coffin home within 2 hours (it can travel up to nine miles) or be utterly destroyed. Further damage dealt to the gaseous vampire has no effect. Once at rest in its coffin it is helpless for 1 hour, then resumes healing.

Gaseous Form (Su): As a standard action, a vampire can assume gaseous form at will as the spell (caster level 5th), but it can remain gaseous indefinitely and has a fly speed of 20 feet with perfect maneuverability.

Spider Climb (Ex): A vampire can climb sheer surfaces as though with a spider climb spell.

Turn Resistance (Ex): A vampire has +4 turn resistance.

Weaknesses: Vampires cannot tolerate garlic and recoil from mirrors and strongly presented holy symbols, staying at least 5 feet away and unable to attack the bearer for the encounter. They cannot cross running water unless carried, and cannot enter a home unless invited.

Slaying a Vampire: Direct sunlight disorients a vampire: it can take only a single move or attack action and is destroyed utterly the next round if it cannot escape. Immersion in running water destroys it at the end of the third round. A wooden stake through the heart instantly slays it, though it revives if the stake is removed unless the body is destroyed.

lore.summary: The gloom is the apex predator of the hunter's own art — a silent, shadow-walking assassin spoken of in the schools the way villagers speak of the schools' own hunters. It steps from darkness, opens a throat with a single dreadful dagger, and is gone before the body falls. To take a gloom's trophy is the work of a master, and the unique rumor your own page on it should remain humble before.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Man-shaped, but wrought of living shadow.
Durability: Hard almost beyond reckoning; only the mightiest weapons and magic touch it at all.
Defenses: Mundane and even lesser-enchanted steel slides off it.
Speed: Faster than thought — it steps from shadow to shadow and strikes before you know it's there.
Might: A single dreadful dagger-stroke can open a hero's throat outright.
Mind: Brilliant, silent and merciless — the apex of the hunter's own art turned predator.
Disposition: A pure assassin; total ambush, then gone before the body falls.
Bane: Light; it cannot walk shadows that aren't there.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It walks the shadows under a shroud of perfect silence, lands a terror-gaze and a killing strike that can fell a champion in one blow, then vanishes back into darkness to do it again. It is the nightmare even hunters whisper about.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• NOT a beginner's trophy. I've buried three who thought otherwise. LIGHT THE ROOM. –the Warden
• If the room goes silent, you're already in its reach.
• Only the greatest arms even mark it. Avert your eyes from its face, and never let it act unseen.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: You will not be offered words. If a gloom has been sent for you, the conversation already happened elsewhere, over your name. Move, hide, and break the one who holds the contract.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Legendary — A legendary terror

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Monstrous Humanoid
Initiative: +26 (+18 Dex, +8 Superior Initiative)
Speed: 30 ft.
Armor Class: 40 (+18 Dex, +12 insight), touch 40, flat-footed 22
Base Attack/Grapple: +25/+36
Attack: +10 keen dagger of human dread +54 (1d4+21/17-20) melee
Full Attack: +10 keen dagger of human dread +54/+49/+44/+39 (1d4+21/17-20) melee
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Fear gaze, sneak attack +13d6
Special Qualities: Blindsight 60 ft., opportunist, quiescence, spell-like abilities, SR 35, DR 10/epic
Saves: Fort +17, Ref +32, Will +21
Abilities: Str 32, Dex 46, Con 29, Int 26, Wis 25, Cha 30
Skills: Bluff +38, Climb +39, Hide +46, Intimidate +38, Jump +39, Listen +35, Move Silently +66, Spot +35, Survival +35, Tumble +46
Feats: Dodge, Improved Initiative, Improved Critical (dagger), Mobility, Sneak Attack of Opportunity, Spring Attack, Superior Initiative, Weapon Finesse, Weapon Focus (dagger)
Environment: Any urban
Organization: Solitary
Challenge Rating: 25
Alignment: Usually lawful evil

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Fear Gaze: Viewing the gloom’s face inspires terror. Creatures that meet the gloom’s gaze must succeed at a Will save (DC 32) or suffer the effects of a fear spell as cast by a 20th-level caster. The DC is Charisma-based.

Opportunist: This ability functions like the rogue class feature of the same name.

Sneak Attack: A gloom is able to sneak attack as a 25th-level rogue, dealing 13d6 extra Damage.

Quiescence: A gloom is constantly silent, as per the silence spell, although the area does not extend beyond the creature itself. This quality gives it a +20 racial bonus on Move Silently checks (it is still possible for a gloom to create noise, such as by bumping into something that scrapes on the floor or by sounding a chime). The gloom can lower this effect at will.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will—shadow walk; 3/day—true strike. Caster level 20th; save DC 20 + spell level. The DC is Charisma-based.

lore.summary: Older than the surface kingdoms, the aboleth is a serpent-eyed horror of the lightless deep — a slimy, fish-tailed tyrant that remembers the world before the gods and rules slaves with a thought. It does not fight so much as command, weaving illusions while its enslaved puppets bleed for it.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Huge — an ancient fish-like horror longer than a boat.
Durability: Tough and ancient; it weathers much.
Defenses: Slimy and thick-bodied, but its real defenses are slavery and illusion, not armour.
Speed: A terror in the water, near-helpless and crawling on land.
Might: Powerful tentacles, and a slime that curses living flesh to need water to survive.
Mind: Older than kingdoms and monstrously clever — it remembers the world before the gods.
Disposition: A tyrant, not a brawler; it enslaves and deceives and lets its thralls bleed for it.
Bane: On dry land it can scarcely move.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It seizes the strongest mind and makes a slave of it, screens itself behind illusions, and lets enslaved puppets and its own tentacles do the killing — always fighting from deep water where it is swift and you are not.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• It'll turn your own champion on you before you land a blow. Ward the minds first. –the Warden
• Get it out of the water. On land it's a beached, angry fish.
• Ignore the visions — they're cover. Keep slimed friends wet till they're cured.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: It speaks straight into the mind, and it is older than your nation's tongue. It bargains as a farmer bargains over cattle. I treated with one to free three slaves; some nights I still hear it. Only a desperate hunter parleys here.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave danger

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Huge Aberration (Aquatic)
Initiative: +1
Speed: 10 ft. (2 squares), swim 60 ft.
Armor Class: 16 (–2 size, +1 Dex, +7 natural), touch 9, flat-footed 15
Base Attack/Grapple: +6/+22
Attack: Tentacle +12 melee (1d6+8 plus slime)
Full Attack: 4 tentacles +12 melee (1d6+8 plus slime)
Space/Reach: 15 ft./10 ft.
Special Attacks: Enslave, psionics, slime
Special Qualities: Aquatic subtype, darkvision 60 ft., mucus cloud
Saves: Fort +7, Ref +3, Will +11
Abilities: Str 26, Dex 12, Con 20, Int 15, Wis 17, Cha 17
Skills: Concentration +16, Knowledge (any one) +13, Listen +16, Spot +16, Swim +8
Feats: Alertness, Combat Casting, Iron Will
Environment: Underground
Organization: Solitary, brood (2–4), or slaver brood (1d3+1 plus 7–12 skum)
Challenge Rating: 7
Alignment: Usually lawful evil

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Enslave: Three times per day, an aboleth can attempt to enslave any one living creature within 30 feet. The target must succeed on a DC 17 Will save or be affected as though by a dominate person spell (caster level 16th). An enslaved creature obeys the aboleth’s telepathic commands until freed by remove curse, and can attempt a new Will save every 24 hours to break free.

Psionics: At will—hypnotic pattern (DC 15), illusory wall (DC 17), mirage arcana (DC 18), persistent image (DC 18), programmed image (DC 19), project image (DC 20), veil (DC 19). Effective caster level 16th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Slime: A blow from an aboleth’s tentacle can cause a terrible affliction. A creature hit by a tentacle must succeed on a DC 19 Fortitude save or begin to transform over the next 1d4+1 minutes, the skin gradually becoming a clear, slimy membrane. An afflicted creature must remain moistened with cool, fresh water or take 1d12 points of damage every 10 minutes.

Mucus Cloud: An aboleth underwater surrounds itself with a viscous cloud of mucus roughly 1 foot thick. Any creature coming into contact with and inhaling this substance must succeed on a DC 19 Fortitude save or lose the ability to breathe air for the next 3 hours. An affected creature suffocates in 2d6 minutes if removed from the water.

lore.summary: A lurching, three-armed cousin of the giants, the athach is a stupid, deformed brute that haunts hills and caverns, smashing prey with a fistful of morningstars and finishing it with a venomous bite. It is muscle and malice with almost nothing behind the eyes.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Huge — a lurching, deformed cousin of the giants.
Durability: Very hardy; a great deal of punishment to bring down.
Defenses: Thick hide, no true armour.
Speed: Lumbering but long-striding.
Might: Brutally strong — three arms means three crushing blows at once, and a venomous bite besides.
Mind: Stupid, malformed, barely more than a beast.
Disposition: Hostile and dim; it wades in and pulps whatever it can reach.
Bane: Dull and weak-willed; its mind breaks before its body.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It overwhelms with sheer output — three weapons swinging plus a poisoned bite from a second mouth — and out-fights most lone foes. The venom, more than the clubs, is what kills.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Three clubs looks scary. The BITE is what kills you. Watch the second mouth.
• Dumb as a post. One good confusion and it'll club itself.
• Keep an antidote handy and chip it from range — it can't reach far.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Dim, greedy, and at heart a coward. It can be bought off with cattle or frightened off by a show of pain — hurt it early and loudly. Talk in short words. Do not turn your back.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave danger

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Huge Aberration
Initiative: +1
Speed: 35 ft. in hide armor (7 squares); base speed 50 ft.
Armor Class: 20 (–2 size, +1 Dex, +3 hide armor, +8 natural), touch 9, flat-footed 19
Base Attack/Grapple: +10/+26
Attack: Morningstar +16 melee (3d6+8) or rock +9 ranged (2d6+8)
Full Attack: Morningstar +12/+7 melee (3d6+8), and 2 morningstars +12 melee (3d6+4), and bite +12 melee (2d8+4 plus poison); or rock +5 ranged (2d6+8), and 2 rocks +5 ranged (2d6+4)
Space/Reach: 15 ft./15 ft.
Special Attacks: Poison
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft.
Saves: Fort +9, Ref +5, Will +10
Abilities: Str 26, Dex 13, Con 21, Int 7, Wis 12, Cha 6
Skills: Climb +9, Jump +18, Listen +7, Spot +7
Feats: Alertness, Cleave, Multiweapon Fighting, Power Attack, Weapon Focus (bite)
Environment: Temperate hills
Organization: Solitary, gang (2–4), or tribe (7–12)
Challenge Rating: 8
Alignment: Often chaotic evil

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body: Poison: Injury, Fortitude DC 22, initial damage 1d6 Str, secondary damage 2d6 Str. The save DC is Constitution-based.

lore.summary: A monstrous lobster-thing with a mouth of writhing feelers, the chuul lurks in lake, sewer, and flooded ruin. It seizes prey in great claws, drags it to the paralytic tentacles, and eats at leisure while the victim lies frozen and aware.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a monstrous lobster-thing taller than a man.
Durability: Heavily armoured and hard to fell.
Defenses: A thick crustacean shell turns many blows.
Speed: Steady on land, sluggish in the water for all that it lurks there.
Might: Great crushing claws that seize and constrict.
Mind: Cold and patient, animal-cunning.
Disposition: An ambush predator; it grabs one victim, holds it, and feeds at leisure.
Bane: Its paralysis is the whole danger; stay unheld.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It lunges from the water, catches a victim in its claws, crushes them, and feeds them to a mass of paralytic feelers around its mouth — leaving the prey frozen and aware while it eats. It removes one quarry from the fight entirely.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Once it grabs you, you're frozen meat. Don't get grabbed. Simple as that.
• Poison's wasted on it. Bring blades and distance.
• If it seizes a friend, free them NOW — it eats the helpless.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: It understands speech, I am certain — and does not care. To it the speaking races are prey and provender. No terms. Fight it ashore, never in the shallows.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave danger

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Aberration (Aquatic)
Initiative: +7
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares), swim 20 ft.
Armor Class: 22 (–1 size, +3 Dex, +10 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 19
Base Attack/Grapple: +8/+17
Attack: Claw +12 melee (2d6+5)
Full Attack: 2 claws +12 melee (2d6+5)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Constrict 3d6+5, improved grab, paralytic tentacles
Special Qualities: Amphibious, darkvision 60 ft., immunity to poison
Saves: Fort +7, Ref +6, Will +9
Abilities: Str 20, Dex 16, Con 18, Int 10, Wis 14, Cha 5
Skills: Hide +13, Listen +11, Spot +11, Swim +13
Feats: Alertness, Blind Fight, Combat Reflexes, Improved Initiative
Environment: Temperate marshes
Organization: Solitary, pair, or pack (3–5)
Challenge Rating: 7
Alignment: Usually chaotic evil

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Constrict: On a successful grapple check, a chuul deals 3d6+5 points of damage.

Improved Grab: To use this ability, a chuul must hit with a claw attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and can constrict or on its next turn transfer a grabbed opponent to its tentacles.

Paralytic Tentacles: A chuul can transfer grabbed victims from a claw to its ten- tacles as a move action. The tentacles grapple with the same strength as the claw but deal no damage. However, they exude a paralytic secretion. Anyone held in the tentacles must succeed on a DC 19 Fortitude save each round on the chuul’s turn or be paralyzed for 6 rounds. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Amphibious: Although chuuls are aquatic, they can survive indefinitely on land.

lore.summary: A cloaker hangs among the ceiling-shadows of deep places, indistinguishable from a hide cloak or a swatch of darkness until it drops onto a passerby and folds them into itself. Its moan turns a party's nerve to water before the killing even starts.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a thing like a living black cloak or manta.
Durability: Frail once revealed and lit.
Defenses: No real toughness; it hides rather than endures.
Speed: Crawls on the ground, glides well in the air.
Might: A heavy tail and bite, and a smothering body that folds around prey.
Mind: Clever and patient.
Disposition: A ceiling-ambusher that drops on a passer-by and folds them into itself.
Bane: Bright light undoes its shadow-tricks.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It hangs overhead as a patch of darkness, drops onto one victim, unnerves the party with a subsonic moan that breeds fear and nausea, then wraps and isolates its prey while it twists the shadows to confuse the rescuers.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• The cloak on the wall is the monster. Always the cloak on the wall. –the Warden
• Bring a sunrod and a friend who can cast silence — its moan is half the fight.
• Watch the ceiling before it drops.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Its kind do speak — in sighs and shudders of the flesh, a tongue no hunter learns in one lifetime — and their purposes are not ours. In the dark it is already above you. Treat every meeting as the ambush it is.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Aberration
Initiative: +7
Speed: 10 ft. (2 squares), fly 40 ft. (average)
Armor Class: 19 (–1 size, +3 Dex, +7 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 16
Base Attack/Grapple: +4/+13
Attack: Tail slap +8 melee (1d6+5)
Full Attack: Tail slap +8 melee (1d6+5) and bite +3 melee (1d4+2)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./10 ft. (5 ft. with bite)
Special Attacks: Moan, engulf
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., shadow shift
Saves: Fort +5, Ref +5, Will +7
Abilities: Str 21, Dex 16, Con 17, Int 14, Wis 15, Cha 15
Skills: Hide +8, Listen +13, Move Silently +12, Spot +13
Feats: Alertness, Combat Reflexes, Improved Initiative
Environment: Underground
Organization: Solitary, mob (3–6), or flock (7–12)
Challenge Rating: 5
Alignment: Usually chaotic neutral

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Moan: A cloaker can emit a dangerous subsonic moan as a standard action. By changing the frequency, the cloaker can cause one of four effects. Cloakers are immune to these sonic, mindaffecting attacks. Unless otherwise specified, a creature that successfully saves against one of these effects cannot be affected by the same moan effect from the same cloaker for 24 hours.

Engulf: A cloaker can try to wrap a Medium or smaller creature in its body as a standard action. The cloaker attempts a grapple that does not provoke an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and bites the engulfed victim with a +4 bonus on its attack roll. It can still use its whiplike tail to strike at other targets.

Shadow Shift: A cloaker can manipulate shadows. This ability is effective only in shadowy areas and has three possible effects.

Moan — Unnerve: Anyone within a 60-foot spread automatically takes a –2 penalty on attack and damage rolls. Those forced to hear the moan for more than 6 consecutive rounds must succeed on a DC 15 Will save or enter a trance, unable to attack or defend themselves until the moaning stops.

Moan — Fear: Anyone within a 30-foot spread must succeed on a DC 15 Will save or become panicked for 2 rounds.

Moan — Nausea: Anyone in a 30-foot cone must succeed on a DC 15 Fortitude save or be overcome by nausea and weakness, falling prone and becoming nauseated for 1d4+1 rounds.

Moan — Stupor: A single creature within 30 feet must succeed on a DC 15 Fortitude save or be affected as though by a hold monster spell for 5 rounds. Even after a successful save, the creature must repeat the save if the cloaker uses this effect again.

Shadow Shift — Effects: Obscure Vision: the cloaker gains concealment (20% miss chance) for 1d4 rounds. Dancing Images: duplicates the effect of a mirror image spell (1d4 images, caster level 6th). Silent Image: duplicates the effect of a silent image spell (DC 15, caster level 6th). The save DC is Charisma-based.

lore.summary: A vast, flowing creature of the deep earth, the delver moves through stone as a fish through water, digesting rock and metal with corrosive slime. Gentle by nature when undisturbed, it is a catastrophe when roused — erupting from a wall to dissolve armor, weapon, and the hand that holds them.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Huge — a vast flowing creature of the deep earth.
Durability: Enormously tough.
Defenses: Thick rubbery hide; hard to hurt.
Speed: Slow afoot and slow to burrow, but it swims through solid stone.
Might: Mighty slams that drip an acid which dissolves stone and metal alike.
Mind: Clever, and gentle by nature when left alone — a catastrophe when roused.
Disposition: Not aggressive unless provoked; it erupts from the rock to dissolve armour, weapon and the hand that holds them.
Bane: Slow to chase, and blind to anything off the stone.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It feels you through the ground, erupts from a wall or floor, and slams with corrosive slime that eats away gear and flesh, then sinks back into stone to strike again from a new angle.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• It ate my breastplate. Off my body. While I was wearing it. Bring a spare.
• Its slime eats armour and blades — fight with magic, claws, or arms you can lose.
• Get airborne; it feels your feet through the rock. And if it's not your quarry, leave it be — it's gentle unless roused.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: The gentlest thing on the deep roads. It wants ore and rare stone, not flesh. Offer metal, speak slowly in the traders' tongue of the Underdark, and it may even carve your road for you. Fight only one that has been maddened.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave danger

sections.body:

Initiative: +5

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Corrosive Slime: A delver produces a mucuslike slime that contains a highly corrosive substance. The slime is particularly effective against stone. A delver’s mere touch deals 2d6 points of acid damage to organic creatures or objects. Against metallic creatures or objects, a delver’s slime deals 4d8 points of damage,

Stone Shape: A delver can alter its slime to temporarily soften stone instead of dissolving it. Once every 10 minutes, a delver can soften and shape up to 25 cubic feet of stone, as a stone shape spell (caster level 15th).

lore.summary: An eyeless, reptilian horror with a frill of sound-organs, the destrachan hunts by ear and kills with sound — bending its destructive harmonics to crack bone, splinter armor, or shred the nerves of anything it can hear. It is patient, intelligent, and merciless.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Man-sized — an eyeless reptilian horror.
Durability: Frail in a grapple; it wants to be at range.
Defenses: Lightly built; it resists sound far better than flesh should.
Speed: As a man.
Might: Slight in the claws — it kills with sound, shattering bone, armour and nerve from afar.
Mind: Patient, intelligent and merciless.
Disposition: A sound-hunter that stays at range and tunes its killing harmonics to the prey.
Bane: It is blind and hunts by sound; rob it of hearing.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It has no eyes and 'sees' by sound, then bends a focused blast of sound to crack bone, splinter armour, or shred nerves — choosing its effect for the foe. In its own caverns it has no ranged equal.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• SILENCE. A silenced destrachan is a blind, deaf lizard flailing at air. –the Warden
• Can't silence it? Close fast and ugly — up close it's feeble.
• Gazes and illusions are wasted on the eyeless, and it shrugs off sound — bring other harm.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: It is cruel for sport and answers speech with the killing sound. There is no bargaining with a thing whose voice is a weapon. Stop your ears and close the distance.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave danger

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Aberration
Initiative: +5
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares)
Armor Class: 18 (–1 size, +1 Dex, +8 natural), touch 10, flat-footed 17
Base Attack/Grapple: +6/+14
Attack: Claw +9 melee (1d6+4)
Full Attack: 2 claws +9 melee (1d6+4)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Destructive harmonics
Special Qualities: Blindsight 100 ft., immunities, protection from sonics
Saves: Fort +5, Ref +5, Will +10

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Destructive Harmonics: A destrachan can blast sonic energy in a cone up to 80 feet long. It can also use this attack to affect any creatures or objects within a 30-foot radius. It can tune the harmonics of this destructive power to affect different types of targets. All save DCs are Charisma-based.

Blindsight: A destrachan can use hearing to ascertain all foes within 100 feet as a sighted creature would.

Protection from Sonics: While they can be affected by loud noises and sonic spells (such as ghost sound or silence), destrachans are less vulnerable to sonic attacks (+4 circumstance bonus on all saves) because they can protect their ears. A destrachan whose sense of hearing is impaired is effectively blinded, and all targets are treated as having total concealment.

Harmonics — Flesh: Disrupting tissue and rending bone, this attack deals 4d6 points of damage to all within the area (Reflex DC 15 half).

Harmonics — Nerves: A destrachan can focus its harmonics to knock out foes rather than slay them. This attack deals 6d6 points of nonlethal damage to all within the area (Reflex DC 15 half).

Harmonics — Material: The destrachan chooses wood, stone, metal, or glass. All objects made of that material within the area must succeed on a DC 15 Fortitude save or shatter. Only relatively small or fragile objects are at risk.

lore.summary: A drow cursed by Lolth into a spider-bodied half-thing, the drider is a bitter, brilliant ambusher — drow torso atop a great spider's body, weaving webs in cavern dark and raining drow sorcery on those tangled below. Pride and spellcraft make it far more dangerous than its frame suggests.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a drow's torso atop a great spider's body.
Durability: Frail of body for its menace.
Defenses: Some magic slips off it; otherwise unarmoured.
Speed: Quick, and it climbs sheer walls and ceilings.
Might: Weapons and a venomous bite — but its real arms are spells.
Mind: Brilliant and bitter; a cursed drow that fights with sorcery, not strength.
Disposition: A high-ground ambusher; it webs from above and rains drow magic on the tangled.
Bane: Silence and dispelling gut it; it is a mage first.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It webs the party from a dark perch, then snipes with spells and a poisoned bite, using darkness and its climbing to keep the high, dark ground. Treat it as an enemy mage on eight legs.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• It's a drow sorcerer first, a spider second. Shut its mouth and you've won. –the Warden
• Burn the webs. A torch is worth more than a blade.
• Bring light — drow magic withers in the day. Reach it past the web and it folds.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Bitter, hungry, and once a person; both halves can be reasoned with, briefly. Some will trade lore or safe passage for magic. Their spider-goddess made them treacherous — set no trust in the bargain outliving your usefulness.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave danger

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Poison: Injury, Fortitude DC 16, initial and secondary damage 1d6 Str. The save DC is Constitution based.

Spell-Like Abilities: 1/day—dancing lights (DC 13), clairaudience/clairvoyance, darkness, detect good, detect law, detect magic, dispel magic, faerie fire, levitate, suggestion (DC 16). Caster level 6th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Spells: Driders cast spells as 6th-level clerics, wizards, or sorcerers. Drider clerics can choose from the following domains: Chaos, Destruction, Evil, and Trickery. The typical spells prepared shown here are for a drider sorcerer.

lore.summary: The nagas are serpent-bodied, human-faced sages and tyrants — water, spirit, dark, and guardian among them. Some guard ancient sites with noble purpose; others scheme in ruin and swamp. All of them think, scheme, and cast spells, which makes a naga far more than the snake it resembles. Confirm the species before the hunt: the guardian naga is lawful good and may be no enemy at all.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a great serpent's body with a human-like face.
Durability: About as hardy as its size suggests; reach the caster and it falls.
Defenses: Scaled but unarmoured; little special toughness.
Speed: Swift and gliding.
Might: A venomous bite or sting — but, like all its kind, its real power is spellcraft.
Mind: Clever and learned; nagas scheme, study, and cast like sorcerers.
Disposition: Varies by kind — some are scheming tyrants, others noble guardians who may be no foe at all.
Bane: Disrupt its spells and it is only a serpent.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It opens and controls the fight with spells, then closes to bite, sting or spit venom, fighting smarter than any mere serpent. Each kind has its own tricks — a charming gaze, a spat poison — but all of them cast.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• 'Naga' is four monsters, not one. Know which you face BEFORE you draw. –the Warden
• The guardian kind are lawful and good. Lower the bow — that's a temple-keeper, not a trophy.
• Antidote for the bite; steel your will against the spirit-kind's gaze.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Ask first which naga. The guardian kind will talk gladly and mean every word — I kept watch a whole winter beside one. The dark kind talks only to pry open your thoughts. Learn the colours before you choose words or weapons.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave danger

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Poison: Injury, Fortitude DC 16 or lapse into a nightmare-haunted sleep for 2d4 minutes. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Spells: Dark nagas cast spells as 7th-level sorcerers.

Detect Thoughts: A dark naga can continuously use detect thoughts as the spell (caster level 9th; Will DC 15 negates). This ability is always active. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Guarded Thoughts: Dark nagas are immune to any form of mind reading.

lore.summary: A neothelid is what becomes of an illithid tadpole that never found a host: it grows, alone in the dark, into a titanic worm of tentacles and psychic hunger, learning the powers of the mind across a lifetime of solitude. Among the most dangerous quarry on the aberration roll, and one whose exact stats vary by the tome — verify before you hunt. (Stats here are approximate; confirm against your source.)

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Gargantuan — a titanic worm of tentacles and hunger.
Durability: Immense; a great deal to bring down.
Defenses: Thick-bodied and resilient.
Speed: Slow and ponderous for all its bulk.
Might: Crushing tentacles, a swallowing maw, and a spray of acid.
Mind: A lifetime's alien intellect — and a will that strikes the mind directly, not with spells.
Disposition: A solitary apex horror; it scatters minds, then grabs and devours.
Bane: It strikes the mind, not with spells.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It softens the field with a gout of acid, batters and dominates with powers of the mind, then grabs prey and swallows it whole to digest from within. It fights as a thinking, psychic predator.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• The accounts disagree on the details. Pin down YOUR version before you hunt it. –the Warden
• Never bunch up — its acid wants a crowd.
• Stay out of its grasp; the swallowed are digested. Fight it mobile and at range.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: A worm the size of a keep, with a god's mind and an infant's appetite. It knows your thoughts before you speak them and values them not at all. There is nothing to say. Do not be there.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Dire — A dire menace

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Breath Weapon: Cone of acid 50 feet long, once every 1d4 rounds; damage 14d10 acid, Reflex half DC 30.

Improved Grab: To use this ability, a neothelid must hit a creature with two tentacles during the same attack. If it gets a hold, it automatically deals tentacle damage and can attempt to swallow the foe.

Psi-Like Abilities: At will—body equilibrium, psionic charm (all targets, duration 15 days, DC 21*), clairvoyant sense, psionic levitate, read thoughts (DC 17*), psionic suggestion (seven targets, DC 17*), telekinetic force (500 lb., DC 18*), telekinetic maneuver (+4 bonus, DC 19*), telekinetic thrust (500 lb., DC 18*), psionic teleport, trace teleport, truevenom (DC 19);

Swallow Whole: A neothelid can try to swallow a grabbed opponent of a smaller size than itself by making a successful grapple check. Once inside, the opponent takes 2d8+15 points of crushing damage plus 2d6 points of acid damage per round from stomach secretions. A swallowed creature can cut its way out by using a light slashing or piercing weapon to deal 25 points of damage to the stomach (AC 22).

Blindsight: A neothelid can use nonvisual means to ascertain all foes within 100 feet as a sighted creature would.

lore.summary: The otyugh is a tentacled, three-eyed scavenger that wallows in refuse heaps, dung pits, and sewers, eating filth and the occasional careless traveller. Slow and stupid, but its grasp is strong and every wound it deals risks rotting sickness.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a bloated, tentacled scavenger of the filth.
Durability: Modest; it doesn't take much to fell.
Defenses: Thick-skinned but unarmoured.
Speed: Slow and lumbering, with reaching tentacles.
Might: Strong enough to seize and crush one victim.
Mind: Stupid, barely cunning.
Disposition: A lurking scavenger; it grabs the careless from its reeking nest.
Bane: Slow and reaching, but rooted; it cannot pursue.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It lurks in the muck and smells the careless drawing near, then seizes a passer-by with a tentacle and crushes them, gnawing with a tooth-filled maw. Its threat is more the rotting sickness in its wounds and the grip than any raw power.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Lives in the latrine pit for a reason. The sickness is worse than the bite. Wash the wounds.
• Slow as winter. If it grabs you, you walked into it.
• Kite it and pelt it — it's got nothing to throw.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Absurd as it sounds: talk. It croaks the common tongue and wants only your refuse. Many a den I have passed in safety for the price of a dead mule. Bargain from beyond the reach of its arms.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

Disease: Filth fever—bite, Fortitude DC 14, incubation period 1d3 days; damage 1d3 Dex and 1d3 Con. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Improved Grab: To use this ability, an otyugh must hit with a tentacle attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and can constrict.

lore.summary: A rarely-recorded epic aberration — a chitinous, antennae-crowned horror that drains the very essence of the living, growing mightier with each touch. Few hunters have faced one and fewer still have written the page you are reading. Treat every line as provisional and the creature as lethal beyond its already fearsome stats.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Man-sized, but an alien, chitinous epic horror.
Durability: Fearsomely hard to kill; only the mightiest weapons touch it.
Defenses: A sleek carapace that turns aside all but the greatest arms.
Speed: Faster and more agile than almost anything you'll face.
Might: A touch that permanently drains the strength, quickness and life from a hero — and heals the thing as it does.
Mind: Brilliant and utterly alien.
Disposition: A lethal predator; it pins prey and drains it dry at leisure.
Bane: Its every touch heals it; the fight is to stay untouched.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It traps a victim in hardening goo, then touches them again and again — each touch stealing strength and life forever while it heals from the theft — all the while its blinding speed keeps it clear of the rest of the party.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Every touch it lands, it heals AND you lose strength FOREVER. Don't trade blows. EVER. –the Warden
• Faster than you, smarter than the page. Don't improvise this one.
• Strike from range and reach. Bring the means to restore what it steals — some loss won't heal on its own.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Nothing behind those lights answers to reason as we know it. It feeds. Strike first, or be somewhere else.

sections.title: Threat

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Cocoon: A thorciasid can eject a stream of noxious goo that hardens on contact, potentially fixing a subject in place and hindering its movement and actions. Using a standard action, the thorciasid makes a ranged touch attack against any foe it can see up to 60 feet away. If it succeeds at the ranged touch attack, the subject makes a grapple check against the cocoon.

Ability Drain: On a successful melee touch attack with a forelimb, the thorciasid permanently drains 1d4+1 points of Strength, 1d4+1 points of Dexterity, and 1 point of Constitution from the victim. The thorciasid knits its own wounds closed with each successful ability drain.

Energy Drain: On a successful melee touch attack with an antenna, the thorciasid gives the victim one Energy Drain. Each Energy Drain bestowed upon a victim gives the thorciasid +1 bonus to its Constitution that lasts for 24 hours. The Energy Drains similarly last for 24 hours, at which time the victim must make a fortitude saving throw (DC 34) to avoid level loss. The save DC is Charisma-based.

monsters.name: Vermiurge
monsters.senses: darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, SR 34; scent

lore.summary: Called by some the 'god of bugs', the vermiurge is a titanic, many-limbed insect-lord wrapped in a living storm of vermin. It is one of the deadliest aberrations a hunter can name, and one almost no school has a verified trophy from. Read this page as legend with a stat-block attached.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a titanic insect-lord wrapped in a living storm of vermin.
Durability: Tremendous; it knits its wounds and shrugs off much magic.
Defenses: A swirling cloud of insects hides it — nearly half of all blows pass through empty air.
Speed: Swift on the ground and a perfect flier.
Might: A venomous sting, four great pincers and a poisoned bite — and a venom that kills fast.
Mind: Ancient and proud; it terrifies the lesser merely by being present.
Disposition: An apex horror; it drifts behind its swarm and tears apart what comes near.
Bane: True sight pierces the swarm that hides it.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It hides behind a roiling cloud of vermin that foils nearly half of all blows, cows the weak with sheer dread, and rends with sting, pincers and poisoned bite. The swarm is the heart of the fight.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• The bug-cloud isn't decoration — it's half your sword swinging through nothing. True sight or go home. –the Warden
• There's no 'toughing out' the venom. Cure it, or don't bleed.
• Ward against the dread, and bring sustained, mighty blows — it heals fast and turns lesser magic.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: It thinks — deeply, patiently, in ways no man follows. One spoke into my mind once, and the words were shaped like a trap. If it talks, it wants something; learn what, then deny it from afar.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Legendary — A legendary terror

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:

Initiative: +11 (+7 Dex, +4 Improved Initiative)
Speed: 50 ft., fly 90 ft. (perfect)
Armor Class: 40 (+3 Dex, –1 size, +24 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 27

Saves: Fort +29, Ref +21, Will +38

Environment: Any
Organization: Solitary
Challenge Rating: 24
Alignment: Usually lawful neutral

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Aura of Doom: A vermiurge is constantly affected as if by a crown of vermin spell (epic spell) cast by a 42nd-level caster. As per the spell, a vermiurge may completely suppress the aura of insects as desired. A vermiurge’s aura of doom constantly replenishes itself at a rate of 200 vermin per round (unlimited duration).

Concealing Aura: Its aura of doom constantly provides a vermiurge with nine-tenths concealment, so all attacks made against it have a 40% miss chance.

Frightful Presence: This ability takes effect automatically when the vermiurge first engages its aura of doom. It affects only less experienced opponents. The affected creature must make a successful Will save (DC 48) or become shaken. Success indicates immunity to that creature’s frightful presence for one day. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Poison: Sting or bite, Fortitude save (DC 44); initial Damage 1d6 temporary Con, secondary Damage 2d6 temporary Con. The save DC is Constitution-based.

lore.summary: A worm that walks is a spellcaster who delved too deep into vile and verminous secrets, until the body dissolved into a swarm of worms that holds a human shape by sheer will and magic. It keeps its mind, its spells, and its malice, and is desperately hard to put down because there is no 'it' left to kill — only thousands of squirming parts.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Man-shaped — but no man: a swarm of worms in a person's form.
Durability: Desperately hard to put down; there is no single body to kill.
Defenses: A swarm of vermin in a man's shape — no heart, no organs, no single body to wound.
Speed: As the spellcaster it once was.
Might: A grasping, smothering body of vermin — but its true weapon is the magic it kept.
Mind: It kept its mind, its spells and its malice intact.
Disposition: Hostile and cunning; it fights as the mage it was while its worm-body shrugs off what would fell a person.
Bane: Crushing blows and fire; blade and point find nothing.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It fights as the powerful spellcaster it used to be — full sorcery and malice — while its body of worms ignores the blows and hurts that would kill a man, grabbing and engulfing those who close. There is no heart to stab, no spine to break.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• No heart to stab. No spine to break. Hit ALL of it — fire, blunt, area. –the Warden
• It's a wizard first. Silence the wizard, then mop up the worms.
• Sneak-kills, poison, stun — all wasted. Know what mage it used to be.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: It was a wizard, and the vanity survived the grave. It will monologue; let it — every minute of the lecture is a minute to place your people and your fire. Its promises are worm-eaten. It means to kill you when it finishes.

lore.summary: Hags of the grey wastes, come up through the ether to trade. A night hag settles upon a wicked sleeper and rides his dreams until the life thins out of him, and what is left she carts off in a sack to sell. She keeps to bogs, barrows and cold inns — anywhere a guilty man beds down alone.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — a stooped crone no taller than yourself, and that is the whole of the comfort in it.
Durability: Tougher than any woman of that frame has any right to be; she takes a beating and keeps her feet.
Defenses: Ordinary steel slides off her — only cold iron with a blessing on it bites deep. Fire and frost trouble her not at all, nor charm, nor sleep, nor any terror you can raise, and most spells break on her like water on a doorstep.
Speed: Walks at a walking pace — and then steps sideways out of the world and is simply gone.
Might: Her bite leaves a rotting fever in the wound. Worse is the slow work: night upon night at your bedside, drawing the life out of you a thread at a time until one morning you do not wake.
Mind: Shrewd, lettered, patient, fluent in the tongues of the pit and of men alike. A merchant to her marrow.
Disposition: Calm, courteous, and wholly evil. She bears you no malice — she is only pricing you.
Bane: The stone at her throat. That charm is what lets her walk out of the world; take it or break it and she is stranded here, in the room, with you — and a month's labour from making another.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: She opens unseen and unreachable, walking through your walls to look you over before she commits to anything. Then it is curses out of empty air, a hand laid on your sword-arm to unstring it, a bite that festers — and the instant the fight sours she steps out of the world mid-stride and returns at your back. She will not trade blows for long. She would rather come back tonight, when you are asleep.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Cold iron, and have it blessed besides. Plain steel is a nuisance to her, nothing more.
• The stone at her throat is the whole fight. Cut the cord, kick it into the fire, and she cannot flee — everything after that is ordinary butchery.
• She rides the dreams of the wicked and the lawless, not the clean. Sleep in company, and keep a watch who can see into the ether — nothing on this side can stop her once she is astride a man.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Talk is her whole trade, so talk. I bought passage from one on the Vale road and was let by honestly, for a fair price. But she deals in souls and will weigh yours while she smiles at you. Fix every word of the bargain aloud, twice over, and never say the word 'anything'.

lore.summary: A bull the size of a cart, plated in dusky metal scales that ring when struck. It grazes like cattle and kills like a landslide — charging anything that moves, and breathing out a vapour that leaves men standing in the field as statues for the crows to perch upon. Hill country, ruined farms, and the gardens of cruel lords.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a bull grown well past any bull, and heavier than it looks by half.
Durability: Enormous. It shrugs off blows that would fell a warhorse and does not slow for them.
Defenses: Scales of true metal, overlapping; a good blade skids where it does not stick fast. Nothing subtle troubles it, because there is nothing subtle in it to trouble.
Speed: Quick over open ground for such bulk, and it gathers terrible momentum before it arrives.
Might: It gores, and it runs the small ones down beneath its hooves. But the killing is done with its breath — a gout of vapour that turns flesh to stone where it stands, and stone it remains.
Mind: A beast, and a dull one. It knows hunger, territory, and rage, and nothing else at all.
Disposition: Foul-tempered past all reason. It charges first and never pauses to consider whether you were even coming its way.
Bane: The vapour is not endless — it has only a few gouts in it before the bellows are empty, and it must gather itself between them. And it is stupid. It charges straight. A pit, a ditch, a stout gate, a step aside at the last moment — it will run itself into every one of them, gladly.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It opens at a dead run, head down with its whole weight behind the horns, and anything smaller than a man goes under the hooves. Scatter and it wheels and comes again. When several of you stand together it stops short, fills its chest, and breathes — and whoever lacks the constitution to withstand it is left standing in the grass as a monument. Then it charges whoever is still moving.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Count its breaths. It has only a handful in a day — make it waste them on empty ground and a rock.
• Never receive the charge. Stand behind something it must break first, or step aside and open its hocks as it goes past.
• What it turns to stone can be brought back, but not by you and not out here. Mark the spot, note the face, return with a priest.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: None to be had. It has the wit of an ill-tempered cow and none of the patience. I have tried standing still, tried grain in an open palm, tried the beast-charms that quiet a wolf — it came on anyway and took my horse. Strike first, or be somewhere else entirely.

lore.summary: Three heads on one body and no agreement between them — a lion's, a goat's, and a dragon's, each awake and each hungry. It comes down out of crags and broken hills onto flocks, caravans and anything slower than itself, burns what it cannot bite, and drags the rest back to a filthy cave where it heaps up coppers like a small vain king.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — lion-bodied, goat-shouldered, and broader across the wings than it is long.
Durability: Solid. It takes proper wounding to bring down, and it has three heads' worth of fight in it.
Defenses: Thick hide and nothing cleverer than that. It relies on the air, and on your fear of it.
Speed: Fast on the ground and faster in a dive — but a poor turner aloft, all lunge and no handling.
Might: Two sets of jaws and a horned butt that will stove in a shield, and then the third head opens and lets go — fire, frost, acid, lightning or a foul choking gas, according to the colour it was born to.
Mind: Dull, but not dumb. It has the dragon-tongue and uses it chiefly to flatter whatever is stronger than itself.
Disposition: Cruel, greedy and vain — a bully with wings. It picks on the weak and grovels to the strong.
Bane: Its own cowardice. Show it something it judges larger than itself and it will bargain rather than bleed. Failing that, bring it to ground in close country where those poor wings are a liability, and crowd it — the dragon-head must gather itself between gouts, and it is the slowest thing about the beast.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It prefers to see you long before you see it, and to come from above — a dive out of the sun, the breath let go into the thick of the party, then it lands among you and works with lion's jaws, goat's horns and both forelimbs at once. If the fight turns it takes to the air again to circle and spit from a safe height, and if it is truly losing it will run, or else start talking. It is far more dangerous over open ground than anywhere else.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Read the dragon head before anything else. Black eats leather, blue splits the air, green chokes, red burns, white bites cold.
• Fight it under trees or down in a gorge. In open sky it owns you and it knows it.
• It hoards coppers and silver and believes itself rich. Coin buys its attention where a drawn sword only earns its temper.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: It has the dragon-tongue and will use it — but only downward at prey, or upward at its betters. Come at it loudly, in that tongue, as something it ought to fear, and it will fawn and haggle and let you by. I bought a road through the Sunset Hills with two goats and a great deal of shouting. It shadowed us for a day regardless.

lore.summary: A lion's body, bat wings, a man's cruel face, and a tail bristling with iron-hard spikes that it throws like a quiverful of javelins. Manticores speak, and love to — one will chat pleasantly with a man while circling for the shot. They den in hills and high passes, take work from anyone wicked enough to pay, and eat the payer afterwards.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — the bulk of a big lion, and the wings make it look larger still.
Durability: Sturdy, and no more than that. A hard-pressed hunting party can put one down.
Defenses: Hide and distance. Its whole defence is being over your head and out of your reach.
Speed: Loping on the ground and quick through the air, but clumsy at it — it flies in long lines and turns badly.
Might: Claws and jaws when it must, but its trade is the tail: one snap and a half-dozen spikes arrive at once, from far outside any bowshot you can answer with.
Mind: Sly rather than clever. It talks, it counts, it bargains, and it remembers a slight for years.
Disposition: Cruel for the pleasure of it, and utterly for hire. It keeps a bargain exactly as long as the bargain is the better meal.
Bane: The tail empties. It carries only so many spikes in a day and cannot grow more before tomorrow — count the volleys, keep something solid between you and the sky, and when the throwing stops you are merely fighting a large bad-tempered cat. Close country and a roof take away everything it has.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It opens at range, high up and well out of reach, and empties volley after volley into whoever looks softest — the robed ones first. It stays aloft as long as the ground below is open. Only when the spikes run short does it stoop to claws and teeth, and it will break off and climb again the moment that goes badly for it. Fighting one in open country is a long, losing afternoon.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Count the volleys. When the tail stops rattling, charge — it is only a lion after that.
• Get under stone or thick timber. Everything it is good at requires open sky.
• It will haggle. It will also take the payment and hunt you anyway. Pay it, then move at once — and not in the direction you told it.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: It speaks the common tongue and would rather talk than work, which alone makes it worth trying. I have bought passage from one twice. The first time it kept its word. The second it took the horse, agreed the terms, and shot at us from a ridge an hour later. Pay in meat, pay in advance, and be gone before it finishes eating.
